summary_responses.subtopic: Federal Credit Union Chartering & Associational Common Bond Rules
summary_responses.response: The National Credit Union Administration (NCUA) Board issued a final rule amending 12 CFR Part 701’s associational common‑bond criteria. The amendment clarifies that requiring members to buy a good, product, or service as a condition of membership will no longer automatically disqualify an association unless the purchasing is the sole purpose of the organization; such “incidental” client‑customer relationships may still meet common‑bond requirements if they play only a secondary role. To explain this, the Board added detailed guidance on defining a client‑customer relationship, provided examples (e.g., electric cooperatives and a fraternal insurance group), and streamlined the review process for pre‑approved groups. After considering 18 public comments—most supporting the change—the Board made additional tweaks, including greater transparency into how client‑customer relationships are evaluated and simpler procedures for pre‑approved groups while retaining quality‑assurance safeguards. The rule becomes effective on January 4, 2027, and for further information contact John Tamashiro (Director, Division of Consumer Access) or Keisha Brooks (Attorney‑Advisor, Office of General Counsel) at the listed Alexandria, VA address.

summary_responses.subtopic: Federal Reserve Regulation D & Depository Institution Reserve Requirements
summary_responses.response: The Federal Reserve Board is amending 12 CFR Part 204 (Regulation D) to revise how it computes reserve requirements for depository institutions for 2027. For net transaction accounts the reserve‑requirement exemption amount stays at $39.2 million, while the low reserve tranche is raised to $688.5 million—a $14.4 million increase—because total transaction balances grew 2.7 percent over the prior year. Even though the Board eliminated all reserve ratios to zero in March 2020, statute still mandates annual indexation of both the exemption amount and the low tranche, so these values must be applied starting with the next calendar year. The new low tranche takes effect for all institutions on January 1, 2027, and the final rule was issued on December 18, 2026 without requiring a general notice of proposed rulemaking. The changes avoid triggering the Regulatory Flexibility Act and Paperwork Reduction Act and are intended to lessen regulatory burdens by allowing smaller balance levels to have lower or zero reserve ratios.

summary_responses.subtopic: National Securities Exchange Fee Schedules & Lead Market Maker Rules
summary_responses.response: On November 10, 2026 Texas Stock Exchange LLC filed with the SEC a proposed rule change (Release No. 34‑106905) seeking public comment, which will take effect on November 2, 2026. It also revises the Lead Market Maker Program definitions—changing “Size Near the Inside” to require minimum notional within 0.25% of the NBBO for 95% of the day and redefining “Time at NBBO” as the average percentage of time quoted at each side with at least $10,000 notional—and adds notes clarifying how missing or invalid SIP NBBO periods and leverage factors affect thresholds. The Exchange says these fee and definition changes are designed to encourage members to provide displayed liquidity, deepen markets, and give competitors less favorable pricing, while staying consistent with the Exchange Act’s requirements for fair treatment of members and investors. In total, the SEC has issued a notice soliciting comments on the exchange’s effort to adjust transaction costs and market‑making standards to promote greater trading activity and price discovery.

summary_responses.subtopic: Medicare Hospital Insurance Deductible & Extended Care Coinsurance Determinations
summary_responses.response:
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), part of HHS, issued a notice (CMS‑8092‑N, RIN 0938‑AV84) announcing the inpatient hospital deductible and hospital and extended‑care service coinsurance amounts for Medicare Part A in calendar year 2027.  
For CY 2027 the inpatient hospital deductible will be **$1,776**—up from $1,736 in 2026—and the daily coinsurance amounts will be **$444** for days 61‑90 of each benefit period, **$888** for lifetime reserve days, and **$222** for days 21‑100 of skilled‑nursing‑facility extended care within a benefit period.  
These figures follow the statutory computation, which adjusts the prior year’s deductible by a payment‑weighted average increase of **2.32%** after subtracting a small real‑casemix effect, yielding the $1,776 deductible and the fixed percentages (one‑fourth, one‑half, one‑eighth) that determine the daily coinsurance values.

summary_responses.response: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is proposing a new airworthiness directive under 14 CFR Part 39 to correct an unsafe condition on several Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model EC135 and EC635 helicopters. This proposal follows EASA AD 2020‑0102, which found that the manufacturer’s service material does not give complete instructions for inspecting the tail‑rotor control system after a hard landing, potentially allowing missed detection of damage. The FAA’s NPRM requires a one‑time inspection of the tail‑rotor control system within 12 months, appropriate corrective actions, and revisions to the aircraft maintenance manual, continued airworthiness information and any approved maintenance or inspection program. It covers serial numbers up to 1276 for the EC135P1, P2, P2+, P3, T1, T2, T2+, T3 and EC635T2+ models, affecting roughly 289 U.S.‑registered helicopters with estimated compliance costs of about $340 per inspection and $85 for program updates. The agency asks for comments by January 4 2027 through the eRulemaking portal, fax, mail or hand delivery, and certifies the rule will not be a “significant regulatory action” nor have a major economic impact.
